traditional_guideline: Ayurveda identifies Nidra (sleep) alongside Ahara (food) and Brahmacharya (restraint/energy conservation) as the three foundational pillars of life (Trayopasthambha). Inadequate sleep provokes Vata and depletes Ojas (immunity/vitality).
recommendation_text: Prioritize establishing a restful 7 to 8-hour sleep sanctuary. Discontinue active digital screens at least 60 minutes prior to rest and consider a warm foot massage (Padabhyanga) with sesame oil before bed to calm agitated Vata dosha.
explainability_reason: Triggered because your reported sleep duration is under 6.5 hours. In classical IKS physiology, insufficient restorative sleep creates dry and irregular Vata disturbances that sap vitality and impair next-day cognitive agility.

traditional_guideline: Ratricharya dictates retiring before the Pitta circadian cycle begins (approx 10:00 PM - 2:00 AM). Staying awake late causes nighttime heat, hyperactive mental churn, and delayed metabolic repair.
recommendation_text: Gradually bring your bedtime closer to 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM. The early night hours are governed by Kapha stability, facilitating deep cellular repair and authentic sleep architecture.
explainability_reason: Triggered because your reported bedtime is after 11:30 PM. Sleeping during the late-night Pitta surge can lead to interrupted sleep, morning grogginess, and ungrounded energy.

traditional_guideline: Charaka defines Vyayama as bodily action bringing stability and strength (Sthirya and Bala). Ayurveda advises exercising up to half of one's capacity (Ardhshakti), without straining into severe breathlessness or exhaustion.
recommendation_text: Incorporate 30 to 45 minutes of light-to-moderate morning movement, such as Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutations), brisk walking, or gentle joint rotations (Sukshma Vyayama).
explainability_reason: Triggered because your reported physical activity is below 30 minutes daily. Ancient texts state that regular mindful movement stokes digestive Agni, reduces lethargy (Tamas), and keeps joint srotas supple.

traditional_guideline: Ayurveda approaches mental equilibrium through Sattvavajaya (mental discipline) and Sadvritta (harmonious ethical conduct). Emotional turbulence and chronic mental pressure aggravate Prana Vata and Sadhaka Pitta.
recommendation_text: Practice 10 to 15 minutes of Nadi Shodhana (Alternate Nostril Pranayama) and cooling breathwork (Sheetali/Bhramari) upon waking or before evening meals to pacify autonomic tension.
explainability_reason: Triggered because your reported stress level is elevated (>= 7/10). In IKS principles, persistent high tension constricts subtle biological channels (Manovaha Srotas) and compromises restful mental clarity.

traditional_guideline: Ancient philosophy emphasizes that continuous uninterrupted mental exertion without contemplative rest drains mental clarity (Sattva) and induces mental turbidity (Rajas/Tamas).
recommendation_text: Dedicate at least one 15-minute conscious unplugged pause into your daily routine—such as mindful nature walking, contemplative breath counting, or listening to calming ragas.
explainability_reason: Triggered because you noted no regular dedicated relaxation practice. Even a brief daily mindfulness pause acts as a psychological buffer that recalibrates the autonomic nervous system.

traditional_guideline: Ayurveda emphasizes mindful fluid consumption rather than indiscriminate over-drinking. Water should ideally be lukewarm or room temperature (Ushnodaka) to stimulate Agni and clear metabolic toxins (Aama).
recommendation_text: Increase daily hydration to 2.5 to 3 liters. Sip lukewarm water throughout the day rather than chugging iced fluids with heavy meals, which dampens digestive enzymes.
explainability_reason: Triggered because your reported water intake is under 2.0 liters daily. Insufficient cellular hydration impairs natural detoxification channels (Mutravaha/Svedavaha Srotas) and promotes internal dryness.

traditional_guideline: Skipping morning nourishment when bodily metabolic fire is awakening can provoke gastric Vata and lead to erratic blood sugar and mid-day energy dips.
recommendation_text: Adopt a nourishing, easily digestible warm breakfast (such as warm spiced oatmeal, stewed apples with cloves, or freshly cooked whole grains) within two hours of rising.
explainability_reason: Triggered because you indicated skipping breakfast regularly. In Ayurvedic chronobiology, waking digestive fire requires gentle grounding nourishment to stabilize morning cognitive stamina.

traditional_guideline: Charaka emphasizes that food must be fresh, wholesome, and prepared with love (Satvik/Purna Ahara). Heavily preserved, ultra-processed, stale, or artificial foods generate internal toxins (Aama).
recommendation_text: Progressively replace packaged snacks with fresh seasonal fruits (like amla, pomegranates, or dates), soaked nuts, and wholesome home-cooked lentil and grain meals.
explainability_reason: Triggered because of high reported processed food consumption. Traditional wellness identifies dense artificial additives as prime contributors to sluggish digestion and tissue stagnation.

traditional_guideline: Excessive stimulant consumption overheats Pitta and dries Vata, causing artificial hyper-alertness followed by adrenal fatigue, heart palpitations, and fragmented sleep architecture.
recommendation_text: Transition your afternoon caffeine cups to herbal restorative infusions, such as Tulsi tea, warm ginger-fennel water, or spiced cardamom milk.
explainability_reason: Triggered because of high caffeine frequency. Stimulants in excess dry mucosal membranes and disrupt normal nocturnal melatonin release according to integrative chronobiology.

traditional_guideline: Overuse of the visual sensory organ (Chakshu Indriya Atiyoga) creates intellectual exhaustion (Pragyaparadha) and destabilizes the nervous system (Alochak Pitta & Vata).
recommendation_text: Institute a 'Digital Dusk' protocol: apply the 20-20-20 rule during screen sessions and eliminate digital displays at least one hour before retiring to bed.
explainability_reason: Triggered because your daily screen time exceeds 7 hours. Classical texts explicitly warn that excessive sensory stimulation taxes the mental faculties and disrupts restorative sleep.

traditional_guideline: Humans are microcosms of nature (Yatha Pinde Tatha Brahmande). Deprivation of natural sunlight and fresh air suppresses bio-photonic vitality and natural circadian synchronization.
recommendation_text: Ensure at least 20 to 30 minutes of natural outdoor exposure daily, preferably during early morning sunlight to calibrate your circadian clock and support natural Vitamin D synthesis.
explainability_reason: Triggered because your outdoor exposure is under 20 minutes daily. Natural sunlight provides essential ambient signaling for hormonal rhythms and mood elevation.

traditional_guideline: Consuming meals at erratic timings confuses metabolic Agni, leading alternately to incomplete digestion (Ajeerna) and tissue malnourishment.
recommendation_text: Establish fixed eating windows: lunch as the primary substantial meal between 12:00 PM and 1:30 PM (when Pitta is peak) and a lighter dinner before 8:00 PM.
explainability_reason: Triggered because meal timings were reported as irregular. The digestive fire follows the solar arc; synchronizing meals with nature's diurnal clock optimizes metabolic breakdown.
